security_and_data_review: The asynchronous-entity regression fails at column comparison after its parse-status and XML_ERROR_ASYNC_ENTITY assertions succeed. It does not report accepted cross-entity markup.
The internal-entity-closes-DOCTYPE regression rejects before its error-code comparison fails. It does not report acceptance of the attempted source-boundary escape.

The external-entity-values and invalid-foreign-DTD failures shown here are child malformed-input diagnostic mismatches; the tests reach code-comparison assertions, rather than unexpected successful acceptance.

The unknown-encoding callback-protection test deliberately converts a multibyte sequence to ASCII A. The supported contract rejects that alias. This test consequently does not establish its later release/reentry assertions, which are covered separately for supported conversions by lifecycle regressions and the callback-driven ASan campaigns.
Caller salt setters reject unsupported requests, while actual entity/namespace maps use std::collections::hash_map::RandomState rather than an unseeded fixed hasher.

Relative entity-amplification setters reject unsupported requests; this is distinct from the supported live-allocation tracker controls. Absolute family input/expansion/depth/metadata limits remain active.

test_mem_api_unlimited is specifically a tracker-scope difference: after setting activation threshold0, a1000-byte XML_MemMalloc is rejected because Oriole tracks helper allocations. It is not merely the512MiB backing ceiling or an observed corrupting allocation failure.

The UTF8-start-tag failure output identifies only case19, U+0901 at NameStart; supplementary-name acceptance is also intentionally broader than pinned Expat. These are documented name-repertoire differences, not reported acceptance of malformed UTF8.

No previously unreported successful-document data loss, ownership violation, acceptance bypass or memory-safety defect was identified in these observed assertions and associated source paths. This is a scoped negative finding, not proof of absence.
broad_drop_in_blockers: 357 remaining non-allocation configurations and630 allocation-contract configurations remain failures, even where the behavior is intentional or the diagnostic overlay explains a retry ceiling.
Consumers depending on exact malformed error codes, positions, callback fragmentation/timing/partial error callbacks or XML_GetInputContext cannot assume Expat equivalence.

Custom converters that alias ASCII, delayed external-value encoding declarations, broader Unicode names, non-ASCII namespace separators, wide-character and XML_LARGE_SIZE builds have explicit incompatibilities or unsupported modes.

Caller-provided hash salts, relative entity-amplification setters, absolute family/resource ceilings and tracked XML_MemMalloc/Realloc helpers require consumer-specific handling. Large or deeply nested otherwise well-formed inputs may be rejected.
Version structure identifies target API2.8.4 while the string identifies oriole_0.0.1; software assuming matching identity strings/version semantics must account for this documented distinction.
The measured C interface remains about5–11 times slower on generated4KiB workloads. Application capacity/latency needs its own measurement.
Additional distribution targets and final installed-interpreter/PBS validation are separate deployment gates.

bounded_trial_assessment.assessment: The retained evidence supports a controlled, opt-in CPython3.12.13 Linuxx86-64 trial for workloads within the documented contract, once the exact final PBS artifact completes its installed-interpreter and baseline gates. It does not support replacing arbitrary Expat consumers by default.
support: Actual pinned CPython XML consumers succeed across shared/static and original/fixed cleanup configurations; the explicit cleanup fix remains part of the intended integration.

246 workspace tests, native callback/allocation probes, semantic differential comparisons, W3C acceptance observations and the final3,912,477-execution ASan checkpoint cover the tested bounded deployment.
Source, binary, input and command hashes preserve the exact lineage; failure/skip counts and remaining contracts are retained.
